explanation: Existential statement of Goodman's degree-4 simple-roots example: f is monic of degree 4 with 4 distinct roots, and for some c > 0 the closed sublevel set has 4 components, one of them non-convex. It uses the closed sublevel set of the main problem rather than the strict one of Goodman's displayed examples. Since c is existentially quantified this costs nothing, because non-convexity of a component persists when c is lowered slightly below the merging level.
